prose.text: ZPA limits calls per source IP in a 10-second window and answers 429 with a retry-after header. The ZIA limits are different, in [[zia.api.rate-limits]].

checks.do: Whether bursts of reads exceed 20 in 10 seconds, or writes 10 in 10 seconds, from one source IP.
Whether the client waited the retry-after interval before retrying.

limits.statement: For each organization, ZPA API calls from one IP address are limited to 20 GET calls and 10 POST, PUT or DELETE calls in a 10-second interval.

quotes: all Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) API endpoints called from a specific IP address are subjected to the following rate limits:
20 times in a 10-second interval for a GET call
10 times in a 10-second interval for any POST/PUT/DELETE call

window-start.statement: The rate limits start as soon as the first call is executed, and calls may occur more than once per second within the limits.

quotes: All rate limits start as soon as the first call is executed.
Calls can occur more than once per second, but no more than the limits for each operation type.

retry-after.statement: A call over the limit gets HTTP 429 with a retry-after response header (for example 13s) giving the time to wait before the next call.

quotes: an HTTP 429 response code is returned along with a response header that includes the retry-after field.
the value 13s indicates 13 seconds of wait period
